'''Emara''' officially the '''Emaran Republic''' located primarily in [[South Ayuma]]. Its overseas regions and territories include [[Tiesa Canal Territory|Tiesa Canal territory]], [[Eldas Isle]], [[Weimrino]] and [[Lyters]] in the [[Hinsakian Ocean]], and many islands in [[South Eanif Ocean|South]] and [[North Eanif Ocean]], giving it one of the largest discontinuous exclusive [[economic zones]] in the world. Emara shares borders with [[Siana]] and [[Lycroa]] to the north; Also boarding [[Trian]] and [[Etretes]] with the [[Tiesa Canal Territory|Tiesa canal territory]] and a maritime border with [[Easuhura]] to the east. Its metropolitan area extends from the [[Druvain river]] to the north, [[Vihsanna Ocean]] and from the [[Rianian Sea]] to the [[Escaran Channel]]. Its 32 central regions—1 of which is overseas—span a combined area of 428,786 km2 (165,555 sq mi) and have an estimated total population of over 90.8 million as of 1765. Emara is a [[wikipedia:Semi-presidential_republic|semi-presidential republic]] and its capital, largest city and main cultural and economic centre is [[Rivostan]].

Emara was settled during the [[Bronze age]] by [[Carth]] tribes known as [[Arznx]] before [[Ecossian]] first started settling the east coast in the 5-4th centuries BFA, followed by the conquests by the [[Vestorian empire]] in the 1st century BFA, leading to a distinct Vestor-Ecossian culture. In the [[Early Middle Ages]], the Emarans formed the kingdom of Destria, which became the heartland of the Destrain Empire. The [[Treaty of Abutot]] in 664 partitioned the empire, with [[West Bervia]] evolving into the [[Kingdom of Poime.]] In the [[Early Middle Ages]], Emara was a powerful but decentralised [[wikipedia:Feudalism|feudal kingdom]], but from the mid-11th to the mid-12th centuries, Emara was plunged into a dynastic conflict with [[Easuhura]] known as the [[Two Hundred Years' War]]. In the 14th century, Emaran culture flourished during the [[Emaran Renaissance]] under [[Lycroa|Lycoan]] rule, and an Emaran colonial empire emerged. Internally, Emara was dominated by the conflict with the Lycroans under the [[Friliens]] and the growing religious conflict between [[Inurraconas]] and [[Lengea]]. Emara was successful in the [[Redea Succession war]] and further increased its influence during the reign of [[Zonasa the Honourable]].

The [[Emaran Revolution|Emaran Revolution of 1577]] overthrew the [[Dialxao]] Regime and produced the Declaration of the Rights of All, which expresses the nation's ideals to this day. Emara reached its political and military zenith in the early 17th century under the newly created [[Liberal party]], being the primary force for Ayuman [[wikipedia:Imperialism|imperialism]] and establishing the [[First Emaran Empire]]. The collapse of the empire initiated a period of relative decline, in which Emara endured the [[Sicla Restoration]] until the founding of the [[Emaran Second Republic]], which was succeeded by the [[Emaran Third Republic|Third Republic]] upon the [[Emaran 1644 Revolts|1644 Revolts]]. Emara was one of the major participants of [[Great Imperial War|The Great Imperial War]] from which it emerged victorious at great human and economic cost. It was among the Victors of the [[Red War|Red war]], but it was [[wikipedia:Military_occupation|occupied]] for most of the war. Following its liberation, the short-lived [[Sixth Emaran Republic|Sixth Republic]] was established and later dissolved after military defeats in [[Haiza]]. The current Seventh Republic was formed in 1710. Most Emaran [[wikipedia:Colony|colonies]] became [[wikipedia:Independence|independent]] in the 1700s, with the majority retaining close economic and military ties with Emara. Migoku [[1714 Migoku Election|voted]] to stay under the [[wikipedia:Jurisdiction|jurisdiction]] of Emara, but the election was later shown to be [[wikipedia:Fraud|fraudulent]].

Emara retains its centuries-long status as a global centre of [[wikipedia:Art|art]], [[wikipedia:Science|science]], and [[wikipedia:Philosophy|philosophy]]. It hosts the sixth-largest number of  [[Global Heritage Sites]] and is the world's 2nd leading [[wikipedia:Tourism|tourist destination]], having received 120 million foreign visitors in 1763. A [[wikipedia:Developed_country|developed country]], Emara has a high nominal per capita income globally, and its advanced economy ranks among the largest in the world by both nominal [[wikipedia:Gross_domestic_product|GDP]] and. It is a great power, having one of the [[List of countries by number of military and paramilitary personnel|largest militaries]] and an official [[List of states with nuclear weapons|nuclear-weapon state]]. The country is part of multiple international organisations and forums.
